enhanced.fullText:
The Standards for the Management of Used Oil, codified under 40 CFR Part 279, establishes comprehensive federal requirements for the proper handling, storage, and disposal of used oil across all sectors, including higher education institutions. This regulation, promulgated under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) at 42 U.S.C. § 6901 et seq., applies to universities operating motor vehicle fleets, maintenance facilities, laboratories, or any operations generating used oil.

Higher education institutions typically fall under the "used oil generator" category defined in 40 CFR § 279.20, which encompasses entities producing used oil through vehicle maintenance, laboratory operations, or facility management. Universities must comply with strict storage requirements under 40 CFR § 279.22, including using containers and tanks in good condition, properly labeling all storage units with "Used Oil" markings, and preventing releases to the environment. Storage containers must be closed except when adding or removing used oil, and institutions must maintain secondary containment systems for tanks exceeding 1,320 gallons.

Recordkeeping obligations under 40 CFR § 279.27 require universities to maintain detailed logs of used oil quantities generated, stored, and shipped off-site. Records must be retained for three years and include dates of generation, storage locations, and disposal methods. Transportation requirements mandate that institutions can only transfer used oil to facilities with valid EPA identification numbers, as specified in 40 CFR § 279.24.

Enforcement mechanisms include EPA inspections, administrative orders, and civil penalties up to $70,117 per violation per day under 42 U.S.C. § 6928. The 2020 amendments to 40 CFR § 279.10 expanded the definition of used oil to include synthetic oils and updated labeling requirements. Universities must also comply with state-specific requirements, as many states have adopted more stringent standards than federal minimums. Non-compliance can result in criminal penalties under 42 U.S.C. § 6928(d) for knowing violations, including fines up to $50,000 per day and imprisonment. Institutions must designate qualified personnel for used oil management and ensure proper training on handling procedures, emergency response, and regulatory compliance requirements.
enhanced.summary: Federal regulation requiring higher education institutions to properly store, label, and dispose of used oil from vehicle maintenance and laboratory operations through EPA-approved facilities.
enhanced.requirements:
## Storage and Containment Standards
- Maintain used oil in structurally sound containers and tanks per 40 CFR § 279.22
- Label all storage units clearly with "Used Oil" designation
- Implement secondary containment for tanks over 1,320 gallons
- Keep containers closed except during filling/emptying operations

## Documentation and Recordkeeping
- Maintain three-year records of all used oil generation, storage, and disposal activities
- Document quantities, dates, and destination facilities per 40 CFR § 279.27
- Retain manifests and transportation records for off-site shipments

## Transportation and Disposal
- Transfer used oil only to EPA-registered facilities with valid identification numbers
- Use properly licensed transporters meeting DOT requirements under 40 CFR § 279.24
- Prohibit mixing used oil with hazardous waste or other substances

## Personnel and Training
- Designate qualified used oil management coordinator
- Provide regular training on handling procedures and emergency response protocols
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No routine federal reporting required for generators. Event-triggered reporting includes immediate notification to EPA Regional Administrator for releases exceeding reportable quantities per 40 CFR § 279.22(d).
